capability: Evaluate all seven original generalized distribution selectors.
operation: density expression, integration mesh and z -> Z(z) and Z'(z)
discovery.boundary: Infinite real velocity contour with stated continuation or finite support.

title.zh: 广义等离子体色散函数七类分布
title.en: Evaluate all seven original generalized distribution selectors.

summary: Evaluate all seven original generalized distribution selectors.

identity.definition: Selector densities: delta(v); f=1 on [-.5,.5]; max(0,1-|v|); sqrt(2)/pi/(1+v²/2)²; H(v-.1)exp(-v²)/sqrt(pi); and 3sqrt(3)/(4pi)/(1+|v|³) on |v|<=4. For a jump J at a, Zp includes J/(a-z). Top-hat density sign and incomplete-Maxwellian cutoff jump are corrected from the inconsistent source. Gaussian derivative uses cancellation-free raw susceptibility/moments at large phase rather than subtracting a rounded unit term. Far top-hat values use a convergent inverse-power series; derivatives form real and imaginary denominator components separately before reciprocal evaluation, preserving representable small contour components. Near the center the real response uses real log1p, near edges log-hypot differences, and contour phase uses a single atan2; no complex log1p is used.
identity.direction: Declared inputs to declared scientific outputs
identity.coordinates: Dimensionless real velocity and complex phase or frequency
identity.boundary: Infinite real velocity contour with stated continuation or finite support.
assumptions: Density is real and integrable on the real contour.
No collective-mode uniqueness or certified global quadrature bound is asserted.

inputs.name: z
inputs.description: Complex phase point z in the same velocity variable v as the selected density: Z(z)=integral f(v)/(v-z) dv. For the default Maxwellian exp(-v^2)/sqrt(pi), v is in units of sqrt(2) v_t, so z=omega/(sqrt(2) k v_t); for a custom expression z is omega/k in the units of v used in that expression.

inputs.name: selector
inputs.description: Density family in the velocity variable v, of unit integral except selectors 5 (mass-incomplete) and 6 (truncated): 0 the expression argument (default exp(-v^2)/sqrt(pi), the Maxwellian with v in units of sqrt(2) v_t); 1 delta(v); 2 top-hat 1 on [-0.5,0.5]; 3 triangle max(0,1-|v|); 4 power law sqrt(2)/pi/(1+v^2/2)^2 (a kappa=2 Lorentzian-type density, not a gamma distribution); 5 incomplete Maxwellian H(v-0.1) exp(-v^2)/sqrt(pi), mass-incomplete; 6 truncated slowing-down 3sqrt(3)/(4pi)/(1+|v|^3) on |v|<=4.

inputs.name: expression
inputs.description: Analytic density in v using finite real constants, pi, + - * / and powers, and exp/log/sqrt/sin/cos/sinh/cosh/tanh. Powers may be written ** or ^, and MATLAB element-wise .^ .* ./ are accepted as the same operators.
inputs.constraints: Real integrable density with decaying derivative; no arbitrary code, comparisons, attributes or indexing.

inputs.name: integration_mesh
inputs.description: Feature-resolving finite increasing velocity mesh; infinite tails are also integrated.
inputs.constraints: All material features resolved; no unresolved tail features.

outputs.name: Z
outputs.description: Integral f(v)/(v-z) dv with the declared continuation.

supported: All original selectors 0 through 6, including exact delta/top-hat and cutoff derivative jumps.
Analytic Maxwellian, gamma and custom expressions with Landau continuation; real-contour piecewise distributions in either half plane.
Upper real-axis boundary values away from endpoints and triangular derivative corners.
excluded: Arbitrary symbolic expressions or executable input.
Guessed analytic continuation of discontinuous distributions.
Silent fallback from unknown selector to Maxwellian.
preconditions: Density is real and integrable on the real contour.
No collective-mode uniqueness or certified global quadrature bound is asserted.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for non-numeric or non-broadcastable z, selector outside 0..6, a nonpositive selector-grid endpoint, or an unsupported expression/integration mesh.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: ValueError for a non-finite or otherwise unrepresentable Z/Zp and RuntimeError when the real-axis or exterior quadrature does not converge; no fallback branch is selected.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: RuntimeError when the real-axis or exterior quadrature fails to converge; no unconverged value is returned.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial Z/Zp pair is returned after a failed call.

scope: Independent basis: selectors 1, 2 and the default Maxwellian have closed forms that are recomputed at 40 mpmath digits -- -1/z and 1/z**2 for the delta, -log((z+0.5)/(z-0.5)) for the unit top-hat, and i sqrt(pi) exp(-z**2) erfc(-i z) for the Maxwellian.
The top-hat sign was determined, not assumed: the opposite ordering differs by exactly -1, which a modulus comparison would not have seen.
Zp is checked against a 40-digit central difference of the independently computed closed form, so the derivative is not certified by the implementation's own derivative path.
Test matrix: three complex phase points on each of the three closed-form selectors, including one in the lower half plane.
Failure matrix: one assertion per channel -- wrong delta response, wrong top-hat branch cut, wrong Maxwellian kernel, and a wrong derivative.
Precision budget, written before measurement: 1e-12 relative on the transforms, 1e-9 on the differentiated comparison.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to selectors 1, 2 and the default Maxwellian of the seven declared densities, at three complex phase points each. Established by closed forms recomputed at 40 digits and by a high-precision derivative; measured agreement is at the 1e-16 level for the transforms and inside 1e-9 for the derivative. Excluded scope: selectors 3, 4, 5 and 6, whose transforms have no independent reference here, arbitrary caller expressions, and any root search.
known_limitations: Selectors 3 (triangle), 4 (kappa-2 Lorentzian), 5 (incomplete Maxwellian) and 6 (truncated slowing-down) are recorded as cannot establish: their reference requires a high-precision quadrature with feature splitting that was not built, so their correctness rests on the existing self-consistency tests only.
The closed forms are exact for the declared densities; a custom caller expression is a different scope and is not covered.

example.description: Evaluate one generalized dispersion selector at an upper-half-plane point.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.kinetic.generalized_dispersion import evaluate_generalized_dispersion
r=evaluate_generalized_dispersion(1j,2)
assert r['Z'].imag>0
assert np.isfinite(r['Zp'])
example.expected: Observed PASS: selector 2 at z=i returns a finite Z and Zp with positive imaginary part for Z.

references: Hua-Sheng Xie, Generalized plasma dispersion function, Phys. Plasmas. 20 (2013), 092125 (scientific context)
